column1: # ci-known-red.tsv — verification units that are RED ON MAIN, declared with a date and an expiry.
# THIS IS NOT A SKIP LIST, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS ENFORCED RATHER THAN ASSERTED.
# A skip deletes the question. An entry here keeps the question, keeps running it, prints the
# answer on every run, and adds two rules that a skip cannot have:
#   * A DECLARED UNIT THAT PASSES FAILS THE BUILD. The defect is fixed and the row is now a
#     lie; delete it. Without this the table would silently outlive everything in it, which is
#     precisely how every skip list in every project becomes permanent.
#   * AN ENTRY PAST ITS EXPIRY FAILS THE BUILD. The tolerance was time-boxed when it was
#     granted. Fixing it, or re-declaring it with a new date and a reason, is forced — the one
#     thing that cannot happen is nothing.
# Both rules live in scripts/ci-shard.sh and are covered by ci-shard.test.sh.
# WHY IT EXISTS AT ALL. On 2026-09-10 the `push:` trigger was restored to engine-self-verify
# after nine days off. Four units were red at the time. Two were Linux portability defects and
# were FIXED rather than declared — that is the default and it is what should normally happen.
# The other two are contract regressions in somebody else's live area: red identically on macOS
# and on Linux, so not a CI finding at all, and re-specifying them means deciding what the new
# contract IS, which belongs to the engineer who changed it. Leaving them red would put a cross
# on every commit for a reason unrelated to that commit; deleting their assertions would hide
# two real defects. So they are declared, dated, and expire.
# RULED BY THE LEAD, 2026-09-10, and the ruling is the reason these two rows are rows rather
# than commits: A DEDICATED ENGINEER OWNS BOTH FIXES. Neither of these suites, nor
# shell-worktree-sparse.py, terminalize-agent-worktrees.sh or worktree-transactions.py, is to be
# edited from here — two people editing the same lifecycle contract would collide, and the
# person deciding what the contract now IS is the person who changed it. Both commits below did
# update SOME suites (worktree-transactions, reap-stale-worktrees, reconcile-terminal-worktrees)
# and left these two asserting the old contract, which is why the bisect is unambiguous.
# COLUMNS, tab-separated:
#   1  unit id            exactly as `scripts/ci-units.sh units` prints it
#   2  classified         the date this row was written
#   3  expires            after this date the row FAILS the build
#   4  broken by          the commit proven, by execution, to have made it red
#   5  failing            the case names, so a NEW failure in the same unit is visible as new
#   6  why                what would un-skip it, in one sentence, for whoever picks it up
#   7  when (OPTIONAL)    a shell predicate saying WHERE the row applies. Empty or absent means
#                         everywhere, so a row without it means exactly what it always did. Where
#                         the predicate is false the unit is judged NORMALLY, rule 2 included, so
#                         a host that does not have the defect still gets a real verdict. A
#                         predicate that cannot be evaluated is treated as APPLYING and says so:
#                         failing open would rebuild the skip list one broken expression at a time.
# THE TABLE IS EMPTY, AND IT WAS EMPTIED BY ITS OWN NEGATIVE CONTROL
# Both rows were written on 2026-09-10 and both were DELETED the same day,
# because rule 2 caught them. That is worth recording in full, because it is
# the only evidence that will ever exist for whether this file is a skip list
# or not, and it arrived about two hours after the rules were written.
#   the rows      scripts/lib/shell-worktree-sparse.test.sh        (6 cases)
#                 scripts/hooks/terminalize-agent-worktrees.test.sh (11 cases)
#                 declared 2026-09-10, expiring 2026-09-24, each naming the
#                 commit proven by bisect to have invalidated it (6472bb60 and
#                 2afb9703) and one sentence on what would un-skip it.
#   what happened The lead dispatched a dedicated engineer, as its ruling said
#                 it would. Branch zach-opus-cr2 re-specified both suites
#                 against the contracts those two commits introduced, and
#                 landed on main at b4945c11.
#   the catch     Nobody remembered these rows. `ci-shard.sh` ran the two units
#                 after the merge, found them GREEN, and FAILED the run:
#                   FAIL — declared red, but it PASSED
#                   lib/ci-known-red.tsv declares this unit red and it PASSED.
#                   The defect is fixed; DELETE the entry.
# TWELVE DAYS OF TOLERANCE WERE GRANTED AND FOURTEEN HOURS WERE USED. The rows
# are gone. What is kept is the rules above them, and the fact that the rule
# which removed them is the one that would have been easiest to leave out.
# The next entry starts the same way: a bisect, a date, an expiry, and a
# sentence somebody else can act on.
# (A worktree-ledger.test.sh row, declared 2026-09-10 for git >= 2.55, was deleted on
#  2026-09-11: the bound-members fallback it described read the transaction store, which
#  the CEO's workspace spec removed; bound_members is constant now, so nothing in the case
#  depends on the git version (proven here on 2.52 only). docs/plans/worktree-spec-2026-09-11.md.)
